title: Evaluation of a compiled program circuit
statement: Let $n,m,w$ be nonnegative integers, let $\kappa$ be an inhabited type of instruction kinds, let $F$ map a kind and a Boolean list to a Boolean list, and let $\mathrm{prog}$ be a finite instruction list. Suppose the program is well formed for input bound $n$ and block width $w$, and every instruction has exactly $m$ sources. For valid positions $i<|\mathrm{prog}|$ and $j<w$, and every Boolean assignment $x$ to the $n$ inputs, the circuit associated with position $i$ and output bit $j$ evaluates to bit $j$ of the block computed by running the program on $x$, with missing list entries interpreted as false.
